extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, regulated power companies/utilities, grid operators, EPA regional staff, and other stakeholders participating in CAA section 111 rulemaking and state plan development
extracted.subtask_short: GHG standards for fossil fuel-fired EGUs
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register preamble setting emission guidelines and NSPS under CAA section 111 for new, existing, modified, and reconstructed fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs), including BSER determinations, subcategories, presumptive standards, compliance dates, and reliability/justice considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA must determine the 'best system of emission reduction . . . adequately demonstrated,' taking into account costs, energy requirements, and other statutory factors; the BSER must reduce emissions, be based on 'adequately demonstrated' technology, and have a reasonable cost of control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA may determine BSER measures that improve the pollution performance of individual sources (e.g., add-on controls, clean fuels). BSER can be forward‑looking and may be based on technologies not yet in widespread commercial use if reasonably projected to develop. The most relevant costs under CAA section 111 are the costs to the regulated facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emission limitation determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the BSER is identified, the EPA must determine the 'degree of emission limitation' achievable by application of the BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new sources the EPA establishes a standard of performance reflecting that degree of limitation; for existing sources the EPA includes information on BSER and achievable degree in emission guidelines and directs states to adopt state plans consistent with those guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA may determine that different sets of sources have different characteristics relevant for determining the BSER and may subcategorize sources accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategorization allows different BSERs and standards of performance to be established for groups of sources with distinct characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity requirement for BSER and degree of limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid BSER determination and emission guideline must provide sufficient specificity as to the BSER identified and the 'degree of emission limitation achievable though application of the [BSER].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA concluded the ACE Rule failed in this regard; specificity is required to satisfy CAA section 111 and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS with 90% capture as BSER for existing coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is finalizing CCS with 90 percent capture as the BSER for existing coal-fired steam generating units, with a presumptive standard of an 88.4 percent reduction in annual emission rate and a compliance deadline of January 1, 2032.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found CCS adequately demonstrated and cost‑reasonable given declining costs and substantial tax credits (e.g., IRC section 45Q, IRA). EPA also considered that many units have announced retirements when evaluating cost‑reasonableness and subcategorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exemption for units retiring before Jan 1, 2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing coal-fired steam EGUs demonstrating they plan to permanently cease operation prior to January 1, 2032, are exempt from these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined units retiring before this date generally do not have cost-reasonable options for improving GHG performance; sources must demonstrate planned permanent cessation of operation to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategory for units planning to cease operation before Jan 1, 2039
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate subcategory for existing coal-fired steam generating units that demonstrate plans to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2039.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BSER for this subcategory is co-firing with natural gas at a level of 40 percent of the unit's annual heat input, with a presumptive standard of 16 percent reduction in annual emission rate and a compliance deadline of January 1, 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive standards for natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumptive standards and BSERs for natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units by load category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized routine methods of operation and maintenance (O&M) as the BSER for intermediate and base load natural gas/oil units. Presumptive standards: base load (>45% capacity factor) 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross; intermediate load (8%-45%) 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross. Low load (<8%) uniform fuels BSER with presumptive input-based standards of 170 lb CO2/MMBtu for oil-fired and 130 lb CO2/MMBtu for natural gas-fired sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and BSER for combustion turbines by subcategory
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission standards and BSER determinations for new and reconstructed fossil fuel-fired stationary combustion turbines separated into base load, intermediate load, and low load subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base load BSER has two components: (1) highly efficient generation (based on best-performing units' emission rates) and (2) utilization of CCS with 90% capture; second component has a phase-in compliance deadline of January 1, 2032. Intermediate load BSER: highly efficient simple cycle generation. Low load BSER: use of lower-emitting fuels. EPA recognized lead time needed to deploy CCS infrastructure and set phased compliance accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for large modifications of coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: For coal-fired steam generating units that undertake a large modification (increase in hourly emission rate >10%), the EPA is revising standards of performance to mirror emission guidelines for existing coal-fired steam generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids unjustified disparity between obligations for modified and existing coal-fired steam EGUs. EPA did not revise 2015 NSPS for oil/gas-fired large modifications due to lack of observed or planned modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of rules and components
rubrics_metrics.description: The final action comprises four independent rules (ACE repeal; emission guidelines for existing steam EGUs; NSPS for combustion turbines; revisions for modified steam EGUs) and the Agency intends that each is severable from the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within each rule, components and subcategory requirements are also severable (e.g., subcategories for existing sources; components of base load BSER for turbines). EPA explains practical independence and gives examples demonstrating functionality without other components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grid reliability-related adjustments and flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA adjusted final rules to accommodate resource adequacy and grid reliability needs, informed by comments and consultation with FERC, DOE, NERC, balancing authorities, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments include changes to the universe of affected sources, longer compliance timeframes for CCS implementation, other compliance flexibilities, articulation of appropriate use of RULOF during state plan development, and programmatic mechanisms to address reliability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability emergency mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: A short-term reliability emergency mechanism is available for states to provide more flexibility by using an alternative emission limitation during acute operational emergencies when the grid is under heavy strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A similar short-term reliability emergency mechanism is available to new sources. Mechanism designed to respond to acute grid reliability needs; details and use are described for state plan inclusion and EPA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance date extension for existing sources installing control technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: States may provide a compliance date extension for existing sources of up to 1 year under certain circumstances for sources installing control technologies to comply with standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions exceeding 1 year must be addressed through a state plan revision. For new base load combustion turbines, EPA also creates a mechanism to request a 1-year extension of their CCS compliance deadline under certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism for temporarily retaining retiring units
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include, in state plans, a reliability assurance mechanism of up to 1 year that would allow existing units that had planned to cease operating by a certain date to temporarily remain available to support reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use this pathway there must be an adequate demonstration of need, certification by a reliability authority, and approval by the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator. EPA plans to seek FERC advice for extension requests exceeding 6 months. Extensions beyond 1 year require state plan revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to evaluate resource adequacy through modeling and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA evaluated resource adequacy implications of these actions through a technical support document and capacity expansion modeling to ensure resource adequacy can be maintained with the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA also performed sensitivity analyses (e.g., higher load growth) and finds industry pathways exist to comply while respecting NERC reliability considerations; states and stakeholders should consider these analyses and modeling in planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of federal incentives and funding in BSER/cost-reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered lower costs of CCS and federal incentives (e.g., IRC section 45Q tax credits, IRA, IIJA, CHIPS) that affect the cost-reasonableness and deployment feasibility of technologies when determining BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs can largely offset CCS costs and influence where capital-intensive technologies are cost-reasonable to deploy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of unit operation, retirement plans, and utilization in evaluating CCS feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CCS entails significant capital expenditures and is only cost-reasonable for units that will operate enough to defray capital costs; EPA considered utilities' announced retirement plans and sector trends in determining where CCS is feasible and cost-reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA used observed declines in fossil fuel generation and announced retirements to justify subcategorization and exemptions for retiring units.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan requirement to maintain stringency of EPA's BSER
rubrics_metrics.description: States submitting plans for emission guidelines must maintain the stringency of the EPA's BSER determination when establishing standards of performance in state plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States have flexibilities (e.g., reliability mechanisms, short-term emergency limits, extensions) but must ensure their adopted standards are consistent with the Agency's BSER and degree-of-limitation determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice (EJ) analytical considerations and stakeholder outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered impacts on communities with environmental justice concerns, conducted extensive outreach with Tribal nations and EJ communities, and incorporated EJ analytical considerations and stakeholder engagement into the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with Executive Order 14096 and other directives, EPA's analyses and outreach informed rule design; state plans and regulated entities should consider EJ impacts and stakeholder input in implementation.
